title: soft-strict-schema-negotiation-with-streaming-checkpoints-and-deprecation-messaging
author: Ethan Romero
commits: Initial PR: design and proto for soft-strict negotiation and streaming checkpoints
Streaming checkpoint layer and checkpoint serialization (src/runtime/streaming_checkpoint.cu)
OpenAI-compat mapping for legacy response_format -> response_contract (api/openai_compat/response_mapper.go)
Add opt-in flag and telemetry + unit tests (sdk/python/redwood/schema_options.py, tests/test_schema_streaming.py)
Fix flake in unit tests and reduce telemetry cardinality
description:
Motivation: Users have requested more graceful handling when a model's streaming output cannot be fully validated against a declared JSON schema (response_contract). Strict mode today either accepts or rejects a streaming response at the end, which is brittle for long-running streams and tool-calling flows. This PR introduces a soft-strict negotiation mode that: 1) tries to validate incrementally during streaming using lightweight checkpoints, 2) falls back to a best-effort coercion/diagnostic path when schema cannot be satisfied, and 3) emits clear deprecation and migration guidance for the legacy response_format field.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds a negotiation backoff policy for response_contract validation that attempts incremental validation while the stream is live and uses backoff thresholds to switch to a best-effort mode instead of hard reject.
- Implements streaming checkpoints: the runtime emits small, signed checkpoint markers at configurable intervals so validators can resume validation when partial fragments arrive out of order. Checkpoints are lightweight and storage-backed with TTL.
- Introduces a "soft-strict" flag on the API surface and SDKs (sdk/python/redwood/schema_options.py) that opts the call into diagnostic-rich validation: validation errors are surfaced as structured diagnostics rather than immediate stream termination.
- Enhances OpenAI compatibility mapper to translate legacy response_format values into response_contract hints so older clients continue to behave predictably (api/openai_compat/response_mapper.go).
- Adds deprecation warnings for response_format in server responses and the CLI; docs updated with migration steps (docs/response_contracts.md).
- Wire up telemetry with reduced cardinality: validation outcome (ok/soft-fallback/hard-reject), time-to-first-valid-chunk, and checkpoint-count. Telemetry rules are in observability/telemetry_rules.yaml (opt-in by default).
- Comprehensive unit and integration tests for streaming validation, checkpoint resumption, and compat mapping.

Design notes:
- Soft-strict semantics: by default the runtime still enforces strict schema validation for non-streaming calls. For streaming calls the soft-strict signal allows the runtime to maintain low-latency response and provide diagnostics via a header + final payload field. This preserves signal for downstream tool callers while avoiding hard failures during transient model tokenization/formatting issues.
- Checkpointing: checkpoints are intentionally minimal (seq_id, kv-hash, byte-offset, signature) to allow fast resume and verification without storing full partial responses. Checkpoints are TTL'd (configurable) and not retained in long-term logs.
- Backoff policy: exponential backoff with jitter; after N failed attempts we emit a soft-fallback state and continue streaming. The thresholds are tunable by customer and default to conservative values validated in perf canary.

Rollout and flags:
- Feature gate: runtime config flag "enable_soft_strict_schema" (disabled by default for enterprise Private installs). Hosted will enable opt-in for beta customers.
- SDKs: Python SDK exposes allow_soft_strict=True on the generation call; TS/Go SDKs will follow in a follow-up patch (tracked in ENG-1587).
- Observability: telemetry is opt-in; verbose diagnostics are gated to avoid PII exposure.

Migration guide (short):
- If you use response_format today, update to response_contract by following docs/response_contracts.md. The server will include migration headers for two release cycles. Quick path: set response_contract to a minimal schema (top-level object with optional fields) and enable allow_soft_strict during testing to observe diagnostics.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implementation in runtime + compat mapping
- [x] SDK flag in Python
- [x] Unit/integration tests
- [x] Docs + migration guidance
- [x] Telemetry rule (opt-in)

CI and perf notes: The integration canary run exercised endpoint-level latency and found <2% p50 increase for typical short chat requests; large-token streaming flows saw ~7% overhead when checkpoints are enabled (configurable). Canaries and perf-lab reports are attached to the Linear ticket.

Merge notes: Squashed into a single commit for readability and small revert path. See merge commit for the final canonical patch.

Related: ENG-1492 (streaming schema strategy), ENG-1587 (SDK flags), SUP-4421 (customer incident that motivated soft-fallback behavior).
review_comments: Aisha Patel: Nice incremental approach. Two asks: reduce telemetry cardinality for model_name+schema_id combos and add an explicit opt-out for private installs. Please add unit tests for the checkpoint TTL edge case.
Ethan Romero (author): Addressed in commit 5: lowered telemetry granularity to outcome only + added opt-in flag for enterprise private. Added test for TTL expiry and documented caveat.

Liam O'Connor: Question on security: are checkpoints signed to prevent injection? Also please ensure checkpoint metadata doesn't leak user payload.

Author reply: Checkpoints include an HMAC signature and only store offsets/hashes, not raw tokens. Added unit test to verify no payload in checkpoint storage and updated docs to mention signing (docs/response_contracts.md).

Marisol Vega: Observability looks good; can we gate verbose diagnostics behind a role-based permission?

Author reply: Added check in the console and SDK to require permission 'schema.diagnostics:read' for verbose payloads.
release_notes: Introduce soft-strict response_contract negotiation with streaming checkpoints and backward compatibility mapping for response_format. Adds opt-in telemetry and SDK flags to observe validation diagnostics. See docs/response_contracts.md for migration guidance.
migration_instructions: Enable allow_soft_strict in SDKs to observe diagnostics before migrating. Replace response_format with response_contract gradually; legacy response_format will be supported with compat mapping for two release cycles. Follow docs/response_contracts.md for examples.
additional_context: This PR focuses on production safety for structured output and tool-calling workflows. It is intentionally conservative: feature is opt-in and gated to avoid surprising behavior in strict production workloads. We plan follow-ups to add TS/Go SDK flags and a console toggle for beta customers.
